doc.title: Frank Wess — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: How the Hank and Frank recordings came together via Ilya Lushtak
summary: Wess explains that Ilya Lushtak of Lineage Records, who jams at his home, brought him and Hank Jones together for the Hank and Frank albums.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: You know, one thing that I’d like to look at is some of the recordings that you have made in recent years and I think that probably just before you did your original oral history, you did your first Hank and Frank, Hank and Frank recording. That was in 2002.
Hank and Frank? When was that?
I think the first one was in 2002 and then the second one is more recent, from this past year. Can you talk a little bit about how those recordings came together, how you guys decided to pair up?

A friend of mine, who has been a planner to me, his name is Ilya Lushtak; he’s a Russian young man. He grew up in the Bay Area, but actually, he’s from St. Petersburg. He’s there right now, he just left, and he’ll be there for a while with his family. But anyways, he has his own record company. What do they call it?

Yeah, Lineage Records, yeah. And so, Miles and I were playing together. He comes by my place and we jam for hours. Bass and drums, and we play; I have to play all the time. At my age, if you don’t it goes as quick as it comes so I have to stay active. He comes back quite often and we play for hours. Having had his own record company, you know, he was friends with Hank Jones also, so he’s the one that got us together for that particular recording, “Hank and Frank.”
Can you talk a little bit about with two such statesmen of jazz, and playing in…both of you, while your in your 80’s Hank is in his 90’s if I’m not mistaken.
Can you talk about your musical dialogue in those recordings?
